summary.intent: Fix a regression in writable-shares functionality (test 3.4) that was caught by a proactively dispatched web-e2e run, and confirm the fix is solid before merging.
summary.outcome: Fix committed as 23c915214: added `publicKeyFromIpnsName` fallback in `parseCachedRecord` so writable-shared-folder rows with null `public_key` columns no longer get discarded. All 29 writable-shares tests pass locally, main CI is fully green, and SDK-E2E is 89/89.

repo: CipherBox IPNS names (k51…) encode the Ed25519 public key, making pubKey always recoverable via `peerIdFromCID` — `publicKeyFromIpnsName` is the exact inverse of `deriveIpnsName`.
Writable-shared-folder DB rows have a null `public_key` column; any code that treats a missing pubKey as discard-worthy will silently break writable shares.

web-e2e runs with `workers: 1`, `fullyParallel: false`, alphabetical file order, and aborts on early failures — `writable-shares` sorts last and will never run if `invite-link` or `journey-timing` fail first.
web-e2e is not a required PR check; main CI (Lint, cargo×3, SDK-E2E, jest, typecheck) is what gates merge.
Documented pre-existing flaky tests in web-e2e: `media-preview`, `invite-link 1.1` (account-creation), `journey-timing` (login-to-vault).
`UQ_folder_ipns_ipns_name` dup-key noise appears 48 times in the green baseline — not a regression signal.

code.finding: Added `publicKeyFromIpnsName` as the inverse of `deriveIpnsName` via `peerIdFromCID`; used as pubKey fallback in `parseCachedRecord`.

Phase 60 D-06 fail-closed branch discarded any DB record whose nullable `public_key` column was null; fix derives pubKey from the IPNS name instead. Still fail-closed: malformed/non-Ed25519 names are discarded and the strict client re-checks `deriveIpnsName(pubKey) === ipnsName`.

workflow: Proactively dispatching web-e2e (it doesn't auto-run on PRs) caught a regression that unit tests and SDK-E2E both missed — ship-phase rigor.
When CI only prints failed tests and a suite has cascade-abort behavior, absence of a test in the failure list does NOT confirm it passed — it may not have run at all.
Running the specific failing spec in isolation locally (`playwright test writable-shares.spec.ts`) is the decisive confirmation when CI cascade-aborts before reaching it.
Re-running the old commit 2×/2 to confirm consistent failure (not flaky) before attributing a regression is good practice.
The regression's exact log signature (`discarding cached result` for the folder) made root-cause confirmation fast.

friction: web-e2e's single-worker sequential-alphabetical cascade-abort meant the fix CI run never exercised the regression test — confirmation required a local targeted run.
CI reporter only prints failed tests, so passing tests are invisible; combined with cascade-abort, it's impossible to distinguish 'passed' from 'never ran'.
web-e2e has no test-filter dispatch input, making it impossible to run just the relevant spec in CI.
open_items: Pre-existing web-e2e flakiness (account-creation, journey-timing, media-preview) causes cascade-aborts that hide other test results — captured as todo in `.planning/todos/pending/2026-06-24-web-e2e-flaky-cascade-abort.md`.
Consider adding a test-filter dispatch input to the web-e2e workflow to allow targeted CI runs of specific specs.
